generation.explanation: A Galton board (bean machine) drops balls through rows of pegs; at each peg a ball bounces left or right with fixed probability p. After n rows the ball lands in one of n+1 bins, and the bin index equals the number of right turns — a Binomial(n, p) random variable. With many balls the histogram converges to the binomial probabilities, and for large n it looks like a bell curve (Central Limit Theorem).
